simple.meaning: נֶגֶף (negeph) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Exodus, Numbers, Joshua, Isaiah, beginning at Exodus 12:13. Its contexts include family line, blood, land, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֶגֶף (H5063).

definitions.short: a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease)
definitions.full: H5063. negeph נֶ֫גֶף noun masculine Exod 12:13 blow, striking (as judgment, only P); — ׳נ absolute 12:13 6 t.; — 1 fatal blow, plague , Exod 12:13 (death of first-born); 30:12 ; Num 8:19 (indefinite); = pestilence 17:11 ; 17:12 ; Josh 22:17 . 2 striking , נ ׳אֶבֶן Isa 8:14 i.e. against which the foot strikes and so stumbles (|| מִכְשׁוֺל צוּר ).

occurrences.englishText: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.

“When you take a census of the children of Israel, according to those who are counted among them, then each man shall give a ransom for his soul to Yahweh, when you count them; that there be no plague among them when you count them.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel, so that there will be no plague among the children of Israel when the children of Israel come near to the sanctuary.”
Moses did so. As Yahweh commanded him, so he did.
The children of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, “Behold, we perish! We are undone! We are all undone!
Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, although there came a plague on the congregation of Yahweh,
He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a stumbling stone and a rock that makes them fall. For the people of Jerusalem, he will be a trap and a snare.
